data.name: Yash
data.gender_notes: Yash is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit root ‘yash’ which means success, victory or achievement. This name is associated with the gods Vishnu and Krishna, who are believed to bring prosperity and success in life. The name Yash carries the meaning “Success, Achievement” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Yash usually hope their child will grow to embody success, achievement and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of success and achievement in spiritual endeavors.
data.etymology: Yash belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Success, Achievement.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yash total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Yash is deeply rooted in the Hindu tradition and is associated with the gods Vishnu and Krishna. These gods are known to bring prosperity, success, and victory to their devotees. By carrying this name, one is connected to these divine beings and is blessed with their divine grace and blessings. It serves as a constant reminder of the ultimate goal of life, which is to achieve spiritual growth and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Yash is a Sanskrit name derived from the root 'yash' meaning glory, fame, power and victory. It is a name given to a king or a warrior who is victorious and glorious.
historical_references.context: The name 'Yash' was popular during the Vedic and Epics period in India, and was given to kings and warriors who achieved victory in battles and brought glory to their kingdoms.

historical_references.reference: During the medieval period in India, the name 'Yash' was also used as a personal name for saints and spiritual leaders. It was believed that a person named 'Yash' would be blessed with fame and power in their spiritual journey and would bring glory to their community or society.
historical_references.context: The name 'Yash' was also used as a personal name for saints and spiritual leaders during the medieval period in India, reflecting the spiritual significance of the name beyond its military connotations.
